news.content_original: Home News Entertainment Politics Sports Business iSaturday iSunday Editorial Columnist Search Search Home News Entertainment Politics Sports Business iSaturday iSunday Editorial Columnist Saturday, November 28, 2026 Search Search Home News Entertainment Politics Sports Business iSaturday iSunday Editorial Columnist Copyright 2021 - All Right Reserved Home NewsHealthLagos Seeks Africa-Wide Bioshield Alliance As Experts Advocate Stronger Surveillance, Research HealthLatest News Lagos Seeks Africa-Wide Bioshield Alliance As Experts Advocate Stronger Surveillance, Research by Chioma Umeha November 25, 2026 written by Chioma Umeha November 25, 2026 Share 0FacebookTwitterPinterestEmail 0 •••Unveils Digital Bioshield To Combat Emerging Disease Threats Lagos State Government has unveiled an innovative digital biosecurity framework, known as the Lagos State Bioshield, designed to detect, monitor and contain emerging infectious disease threats without disrupting economic activities and the movement of people in the state. The initiative, which integrates artificial intelligence (AI), telemedicine and digital health surveillance, is aimed at keeping Lagos open for business while strengthening its capacity to withstand biological emergencies. The initiative was unveiled by the Commissioner for Health, Prof. Akin Abayomi, at the 11th African Conference on One Health and Biosecurity, organised by the Lagos State Ministry of Health in partnership with the Global Emerging Pathogens Treatment Consortium (GET Consortium), on Tuesday, November 24, 2026, at the Civic Centre, Victoria Island, Lagos. The conference was themed, “Bio-Shielding Africa’s Megacities Against Emerging Threats: The Lagos State Story.” Speaking on the theme, Prof. Abayomi explained that the Bioshield framework was developed from lessons learnt during the Ebola outbreak and COVID-19 pandemic, particularly the need to balance public health protection with economic sustainability. He noted that shutting down Lagos during a public health emergency could have devastating consequences, considering that approximately 70 per cent of residents depend on daily earnings for their livelihoods. According to him, the Bioshield is designed to ensure that businesses, tourism, social activities and everyday livelihoods continue even during public health emergencies. He identified Lassa fever, dengue, yellow fever, Marburg virus disease and Ebola, alongside genetically modified and emerging unknown pathogens, as biological threats requiring specialised preparedness and response capabilities. The Commissioner identified Lagos’ high population density, rapid urbanisation, extensive domestic and international travel, migration, sanitation challenges and large informal settlements as factors that increase its vulnerability to infectious disease outbreaks. He disclosed that Lagos has an estimated population of about 30.1 million, with an average population density of approximately 6,800 persons per square kilometre, while some local government areas exceed 20,000 persons per square kilometre. He further highlighted the risks associated with the movement of people, livestock and agricultural products into the state, noting that Lagos receives approximately 70 per cent of Nigeria’s international air traffic. He disclosed that the state receives about 1.8 million cattle annually, underscoring the need to extend biosecurity measures beyond human health to include animal and environmental health under the One Health approach. Explaining the operational framework, Prof. Abayomi said the Lagos State Bioshield has two major components: an outer layer that identifies potential biological threats associated with people entering the state and an inner layer that monitors individuals who may develop symptoms after arrival. Its Health Radar platform enables the registration and monitoring of travellers and participants at major events, using WhatsApp, SMS and email to conduct daily health checks for up to 21 days. He added that individuals reporting symptoms are connected to telemedicine services for initial medical assessment, with referrals, laboratory investigations and specialised interventions activated where necessary. The system also uses artificial intelligence to support risk classification and escalation of suspected high-risk cases to the Ministry of Health and relevant public health authorities, with the objective of identifying concerning cases within 24 hours of symptom reporting, where possible. Highlighting the successful pilot deployment during the recently concluded CANEX WKND, the Commissioner disclosed that the Bioshield system monitored approximately 19,000 registered delegates, including 2,298 international visitors, amid concerns about the Ebola outbreak in Central Africa and the possibility of imported infections. The exercise recorded 2,454 telemedicine consultations, 241 clinical referrals and 219 individuals flagged for further attention, while 22.6 per cent of respondents reported symptoms requiring assessment. All identified cases were followed up and closed out, with no severe outcome associated with the suspected high-consequence infections reported. Prof. Abayomi disclosed that the state was working towards Bioshield 3.0, which would strengthen the technology’s artificial intelligence and telemedicine capabilities, improve integration with airports and major event venues, establish sustainable financing arrangements and provide a stronger legal framework. He added that plans were underway to integrate the platform with the Lagos State Smart Health Information Platform (SHIP), while exploring travel insurance and event-based financing options to support its long-term sustainability. In her remarks, the Special Adviser to the Governor on Health, Dr. (Mrs.) Kemi Ogunyemi, described Lagos as a critical gateway for biological threats entering Africa, given its population, international airport, seaports and major commercial markets. She stressed that protecting Lagos was essential to strengthening Africa’s health security, noting that human, animal and environmental health were interconnected and required coordinated action. Dr. Ogunyemi disclosed that Lagos had strengthened its disease surveillance systems, Emergency Operations Centre and collaboration among human health practitioners, veterinary doctors and environmental officers. She also highlighted the Lagos One Health Strategy, approved by Governor Babajide Sanwo-Olu, which provides a coordinated platform for the health, agriculture and environment sectors. She called for the establishment of a continental BioShield Alliance involving megacities such as Lagos, Cairo, Kinshasa, Johannesburg and Nairobi to promote data sharing, joint training and common preparedness standards. Earlier, the Permanent Secretary, Lagos State Ministry of Health, Dr. (Mrs.) Dayo Lajide, said the state’s experience during the 2014 Ebola outbreak and COVID-19 pandemic had reinforced the need for sustained investment in preparedness. She noted that Lagos had strengthened its biosecurity infrastructure, including its Biosafety Level 3 laboratory and biobank at the Infectious Disease Hospital, Yaba, while activating emergency preparedness structures, intensifying surveillance and training healthcare workers following the declaration of the Ebola outbreak in Central Africa. She described the successful hosting of CANEX WKND, with over 19,247 registered delegates, as evidence of the state’s growing preparedness capacity. In his keynote address, Deputy Vice-Chancellor (Academic) of Lagos State University of Science and Technology, Prof. Abiodun Denloye, identified inadequate housing, poor ventilation, unsafe water, poor sanitation, blocked drainage channels, improper waste disposal and environmental degradation as major factors increasing disease vulnerability in rapidly growing African cities. He advocated a five-pillar urban bio-shielding framework encompassing environmental protection, disease intelligence and surveillance, resilient urban design, community protection and One Health governance. He also called for neighbourhood vulnerability mapping, improved primary healthcare, stronger laboratory capacity, vaccination, safe food and water systems, and training of health journalists to promote accurate public health reporting and counter misinformation. Also speaking, the Chief Operating Officer of GET Consortium, Dr. Ayodotun Bobadoye, said the conference was convened to assess Lagos State’s biosecurity capacity, identify existing gaps and develop a strategic framework for strengthening preparedness against emerging biological threats. He emphasised the importance of sustained investments in disease surveillance, laboratory infrastructure, border monitoring, environmental management, community engagement and workforce development, noting that biosecurity encompasses the protection of human, animal, plant and environmental health. He expressed the expectation that the deliberations would produce a Lagos biosecurity partnership strategy with short- and medium-term priorities. Presenting on strengthening medical research and innovation for emerging disease preparedness and response in Africa, the Director-General and Chief Executive Officer of the Nigerian Institute of Medical Research (NIMR), Prof. John Oladapo Obafunwa, called for increased investment in local medical research, genomic sequencing, vaccine development and domestic production of essential medical supplies. He identified inadequate research funding, weak institutional collaboration, shortages of skilled professionals and dependence on imported vaccines and diagnostics as major challenges to Africa’s preparedness. He urged stronger partnerships among government agencies, universities, research institutions and the private sector to translate scientific discoveries into practical healthcare solutions. The conference brought together policymakers, researchers, healthcare professionals, development partners, security agencies and other stakeholders to deliberate on strengthening Africa’s capacity to anticipate, prevent and respond to emerging biological threats. Speakers emphasised that effective biosecurity requires sustained government commitment, scientific innovation, community participation, inter-agency collaboration and regional cooperation to build resilient cities and safeguard public health. news.content: Home News Entertainment Politics Sports Business iSaturday iSunday Editorial Columnist Search Search Home News Entertainment Politics Sports Business iSaturday iSunday Editorial Columnist Saturday, November 28, 2026 Search Search Home News Entertainment Politics Sports Business iSaturday iSunday Editorial Columnist Copyright 2021 - All Right Reserved Home Latest NewsBenue Steps Up Ebola Preparedness, Trains Health Workers, Journalists Latest NewsNews Benue Steps Up Ebola Preparedness, Trains Health Workers, Journalists by Tor Vande-Acka November 26, 2026 written by Tor Vande-Acka November 26, 2026 Share 0FacebookTwitterPinterestEmail 0 MAKURDI – The Benue State Government has intensified preparedness against a possible outbreak of Ebola Virus Disease (EVD), training health workers and journalists on early detection, surveillance, risk communication and safe referral of suspected cases. The State Disease Surveillance and Notification Officer, Aluga Doosuur Maureen, disclosed this during a training and orientation programme for surveillance focal persons and media practitioners in Makurdi. Aluga said the exercise was part of measures to strengthen the state’s preparedness and response capacity following reports of Ebola cases in Nigeria and the subsequent alert issued to states by the Nigeria Centre for Disease Control (NCDC). She explained that the training was designed to equip health workers with the knowledge to identify possible symptoms of the disease at community level, promptly notify relevant authorities and ensure safe referral of suspected cases to designated health facilities. According to her, the exercise was being conducted in phases, with the first session focusing on community-based surveillance and risk communication, while a subsequent session would train case managers on the safe isolation and management of suspected cases. She explained that, “Basically, today is for identification around the community and how to ensure safe referral,” adding that the training was organised with support from the NCDC through the Basic Health Care Fund. The State Disease Surveillance and Notification Officer said about 30 participants were involved in the exercise, including community engagement and risk communication personnel, state surveillance focal persons and representatives of public primary healthcare facilities and some private health facilities in Makurdi. She, however, clarified that Benue had not recorded any suspected case of Ebola, stressing that the training was strictly a preparedness measure and should not be interpreted as an indication of an outbreak in the state. Aluga also observed that the state had also put in place a monitoring mechanism for travellers arriving from high-risk countries through information supplied by port health authorities. According to her, such travellers are placed on a list of passengers of interest and monitored by the state epidemiologist for between two and 21 days, corresponding with the disease’s incubation period, to establish whether they develop symptoms. She noted that no person monitored through the arrangement had so far reported Ebola-related symptoms in the state. The surveillance officer also urged health workers to remain vigilant against other priority diseases under the Integrated Disease Surveillance and Response framework, particularly Lassa fever, which she said was already recording suspected and confirmed cases in the state. She emphasised the importance of early notification, explaining that delays in reporting suspected cases could affect the effectiveness of laboratory investigations and timely intervention. Also speaking, the State Health Promotion Officer, Moses Jukul, urged journalists and other trusted community stakeholders to ensure that information disseminated during disease outbreaks was accurate, timely and capable of preventing unnecessary panic. Jukul stressed that confidentiality must be maintained in reporting suspected and confirmed cases, warning against the publication of victims’ names, photographs or other identifying details. He said such disclosure was unethical, regardless of whether a suspected case had been confirmed. “Confidentiality is very, very important. No person’s name or photograph should go out,” he cautioned. Similarly, the Data Manager of the Public Health Emergency Operations Centre, State Ministry of Health and Human Services, Nelson Uhime, urged community health workers to maintain a high index of suspicion and promptly report persons presenting symptoms associated with viral haemorrhagic fevers. Uhime identified persistent fever, headache, nausea, abdominal pain, vomiting, diarrhoea, joint pain and general body weakness among symptoms requiring medical attention. He advised members of the public experiencing persistent fever alongside any of the symptoms to seek immediate medical care rather than resort to self-medication. The Data Manager also urged community health workers to promptly notify Disease Surveillance and Notification Officers whenever anyone in their communities presented such symptoms. Uhime said heightened vigilance was particularly necessary with the onset of the Lassa fever season, noting that suspected cases had already begun emerging in the state. He described Ebola as a viral haemorrhagic fever that could present with symptoms including fever, headache, vomiting, nausea, abdominal pain, joint pain and general body weakness. Friday Onoja, representing the World Health Organisation (WHO), at the event noted that for now, they were concentrating on Ebola, but “We also want to take this opportunity to see how we can integrate a lot of diseases,” he pointed out. analysis.brief_en: Benue State in Nigeria has intensified its preparedness against a potential Ebola Virus Disease (EVD) outbreak by training health workers and journalists on early detection, surveillance, and risk communication. The training, organized with support from the Nigeria Centre for Disease Control (NCDC), aimed to strengthen the state’s response capacity following reports of Ebola cases in Nigeria. The State Disease Surveillance and Notification Officer, Aluga Doosuur Maureen, emphasized that no suspected cases of Ebola had been recorded in Benue, and the exercise was strictly a preparedness measure. The World Health Organisation (WHO) representative noted the importance of integrating disease surveillance efforts, highlighting the need for vigilance against viral haemorrhagic fevers, including Ebola and Lassa fever.

news.content_zh: 尼日利亚贝努埃州通过对卫生工作者和记者进行早期检测、监测 和风险沟通方面的培训,加强了针对潜在埃博拉病毒病 (EVD) 暴发 的准备工作。此次培训是在尼日利亚疾病控制中心(NCDC)的支持下组织的,旨在加强该州在尼日利亚埃博拉病例报告后的应对能力。国家疾病监测和通报官员Aluga Doosuur Maureen强调,贝努埃没有记录到埃博拉疑似病例,此次演习严格来说是一项防备措施。该州还对来自高风险国家的旅行者实施了监测机制,对他们进行长达21天的跟踪,以发现任何症状。在受监测的个体中没有发现任何报告的症状。此外,该州正在重点关注拉沙热,该地区已经出现了疑似和确诊病例。培训包括基于社区的 监测 和安全转介程序,并计划为案件管理者举办后续课程。世界卫生组织(WHO)代表指出了整合疾病监测工作的重要性,强调需要对包括埃博拉和拉沙热在内的病毒性出血热保持警惕。

“畅读会员”点此登录查看原文链接 Open access 拉沙病毒(Lassa virus,LASV)在西非引起严重出血热,但目前尚无获批疫苗。LASV抗原设计的主要障碍在于,其唯一中和靶点糖蛋白复合物(glycoprotein complex,GPC)缺乏内在晚期结构域(late-domain)基序,无法招募宿主ESCRT(endosomal sorting complex required for transport)机制以完成颗粒释放。在此,研究人员报告一种理性设计策略:通过在LASV GPC胞质域末端附加合成的ESCRT招募盒(ESCRT-recruitment cassette),赋予其自主出芽能力。对由16个构建体组成的矩阵进行系统筛选,鉴定出先导候选VLPdEm5。该构建体整合ESCRT招募盒、优化的弗林蛋白酶(furin)切割位点以及异源H1N1跨膜-胞质域(transmembrane-cytoplasmic domain),以支持高效颗粒组装和构象中和表位的正确展示。通过脂质纳米颗粒包封的mRNA(lipid-nanoparticle-encapsulated mRNA,mRNA-LNP)递送,VLPdEm5驱动高效原位病毒样颗粒(virus-like particle,VLP)自组装,诱导快速、高滴度结合抗体,对六个主要LASV谱系具有广泛交叉反应性,并诱导强生发中心B细胞(germinal center B-cell,GC B-cell)活性和记忆T细胞(memory T-cell)应答。关键的是,VLPdEm5 mRNA-LNP在体内针对假病毒攻击提供剂量依赖性保护。该工作建立了一种有效的LASV疫苗候选,并验证了一种广泛适用于非出芽型病毒包膜蛋白的ESCRT工程化mRNA-VLP平台。 研究背景与问题:拉沙病毒(Lassa virus,LASV)在西非流行,可致重型出血热,估计每年30万–50万病例,住院重症病死率可达15%,但尚无获批疫苗或LASV特异性抗病毒药。糖蛋白复合物(glycoprotein complex,GPC)是唯一中和靶点和保护性免疫主要决定因素,其成熟三聚体构象要求严格、糖盾致密;天然GPC胞质尾缺乏晚期结构域(late-domain)基序,不能招募ESCRT(endosomal sorting complex required for transport)机制,单独表达时病毒样颗粒(virus-like particle,VLP)释放很低。VLP多价重复展示有利于B细胞受体交联;Hoffmann等已证明CEP55来源EABR(ESCRT- and ALIX-binding region)可促eVLPs。研究人员据此设计ESCRT工程化GPC VLP,并以mRNA-LNP(lipid nanoparticle-encapsulated mRNA)递送。 研究开展与意义:研究人员构建16种LASV GPC VLP构建体,筛选出VLPdEm5,整合EPM-EABR、弗林蛋白酶(furin)切割位点RRRR和H1N1 HA跨膜-胞质域(transmembrane-cytoplasmic domain,TM-CT);经体外表征、mRNA/质粒LNP制备、小鼠免疫、细胞免疫和假病毒攻击,显示其诱导体液和细胞免疫并提供剂量依赖保护。该研究建立LASV候选疫苗并验证可推广至非出芽包膜蛋白的mRNA-VLP平台。 关键技术方法(≤250字):以LASV Josiah GPC(GenBank: NP_694870.1)为基础模块化设计16种VLP构建体;用双抗体夹心ELISA(DAS-ELISA)和Western blot筛选颗粒释放;Expi293F表达、超速离心纯化,并以尺寸排阻色谱(SEC)、纳米颗粒跟踪分析(NTA)、负染透射电镜(TEM)表征;ELISA测单抗及血清结合,假病毒中和试验测NT50;体外转录(IVT)制备mRNA,微流控混合制备LNP并测粒径、PDI和包封率;雌性BALB/c小鼠免疫,流式细胞术分析脾细胞,并以表达Renilla luciferase的VSVΔG-LASV Josiah假病毒腹腔攻击和体内生物发光成像(BLI)评价保护。样本来源为雌性BALB/c小鼠。 结果:1. LASV GPC VLP构建体的设计与筛选(Design and screening of LASV GPC VLP constructs):DAS-ELISA和Western blot筛选16构建体,VLPdEm5结合活性最高(AUC 59.7%),野生型GPC很低;EPM-EABR是高效释放主因,furin位点和H1N1 HA TM-CT亦增强。 2. 先导候选VLPdEm5的体外表征(In vitro characterization of the lead candidate VLPdEm5):SEC单峰8.94 mL,NTA平均约150 nm,负染TEM见100–200 nm球形膜包被颗粒和表面刺突;ELISA显示与12.1F、25.10C、37.7H结合EC50分别0.47、0.16、0.22 μg/mL,与8.9F弱(48.08 μg/mL),S309无结合,说明保留多个构象中和表位。 3. mRNA/质粒来源VLPdEm5 LNP制剂的制备与表征(Preparation and characterization of mRNA/plasmid-derived VLPdEm5 LNP formulations):7种mRNA经凝胶见约2500 nt单一条带;mRNA-VLPdEm5的DAS-ELISA与质粒来源相当,单独GPC仅背景;mRNA-LNP粒径约100 nm、PDI 0.10、包封率94%,质粒-LNP PDI 0.27、包封率70%;LNP制剂抗原表达优于裸核酸,空LNP无。 4. VLPdEm5 mRNA-LNP诱导高水平广交叉结合抗体(VLPdEm5 mRNA-LNP elicits high-level and broadly cross-reactive binding antibody responses in mice):mRNA-LNP day28 ED50均值471,day56均值8862;质粒-LNP低剂量后结合抗体延迟出现;day70 mRNA-LNP弱中和NT50约1:30–1:70,质粒-LNP未检测到;day70血清结合六个LASV谱系GPC。 5. VLPdEm5 mRNA/质粒-LNP诱导强细胞免疫(VLPdEm5 mRNA/Plasmid-LNP elicits robust cellular immunity in mice):day70脾细胞流式显示两疫苗组GC B细胞(CD19+GL7+CD185+)频率显著高于PBS;GC-Tfh无显著增加;CD4+和CD8+中央记忆T(CD44+CD62L+)显著增加,效应记忆T呈增加趋势;GPC刺激后mRNA-LNP组CD4+TNFα+、CD4+IFN-γ+、CD8+IFN-γ+显著高于PBS,质粒-LNP组CD4+IFN-γ+显著。 6. VLPdEm5 mRNA-LNP保护小鼠免受LASV假病毒攻击(VLPdEm5 mRNA-LNP protects mice from LASV pseudovirus challenge):BALB/c小鼠(n=5)接种2或20 μg mRNA-LNP后day56腹腔挑战表达Renilla luciferase的LASV Josiah假病毒,连续6天BLI;信号day3峰值;20 μg组day1–3显著低于PBS,2 μg组仅day3显著,day4–6组间无差异;说明剂量依赖保护。 讨论与结论:讨论指出LASV为WHO优先病原且无获批疫苗,GPC糖盾和严苛构象使高滴度中和抗体难以稳定诱导,天然GPC不能自主出芽;VLPdEm5的EPM-EABR使GPC自主招募ESCRT,furin位点改善成熟,H1N1 HA TM-CT改善膜展示;mRNA-LNP可重现质粒表达与颗粒释放。体内结合抗体快速、高滴度且跨六谱系,GC B和记忆T增强,假病毒攻击呈剂量依赖保护;但中和滴度有限(NT50≈1:30–1:70),原文将此与GPC糖盾遮蔽、可及中和表位少且隐蔽、非中和表位免疫优势以及非中和抗体Fc效应和细胞免疫参与保护相关联。局限为仅用小鼠Josiah假病毒而非真病毒致死模型;广结合不等于跨谱系中和;非中和抗体与细胞免疫贡献待明确。研究结论(翻译):综上,研究人员通过在LASV GPC C端引入ESCRT招募基序并结合mRNA-LNP递送,将本身缺乏出芽能力的病毒包膜糖蛋白转化为强效、广泛交叉反应免疫原;系统优化VLP构建体进一步提高VLP产量;这些工作建立可转移框架以改善免疫原性,并为将其他出芽效率低的病毒包膜蛋白转化为自组装、免疫原性mRNA-VLP疫苗提供可转移技术策略。 打赏 展开全文 开通VIP 享海量文章 全站开放获取+解锁超过 200万篇新闻全文+每日更新 2000+篇,学术前沿动态全时追踪! 从2000到2026,27载全因有您;您的每一分支持,都给予我们无穷的动力! 公测期:打赏8元解锁30天免费阅读! 下载安捷伦电子书《通过细胞代谢揭示新的药物靶点》探索如何通过代谢分析促进您的药物发现研究 10x Genomics新品Visium HD 开启单细胞分辨率的全转录组空间分析! 欢迎下载Twist《不断变化的CRISPR筛选格局》电子书 下载《细胞内蛋白质互作分析方法电子书》 引领行业 | 聚焦麦特绘谱代谢组学整体解决方案>> 「大小鼠繁育与健康管理」指导海报,点击即可免费领取电子版或实体海报>> 揭秘单细胞测序-深入了解这项正在改变我们开展科学研究的技术>> 18,000+ 成品模型现货随取,点击下载模式生物选型指南>> 相关新闻 生物通微信公众号 生物通新浪微博 微信 新浪微博 我要投稿 搜索 国际 国内 人物 产业 热点 科普 热搜:拉沙病毒(LASV)|糖蛋白复合物(GPC)|病毒样颗粒(VLP)|ESCRT招募基序|mRNA-脂质纳米颗粒(mRNA-LNP)|体液与细胞免疫 热点排行 今日动态 | 人才市场 | 新技术专栏 | 中国科学人 | 云展台 | BioHot | 云讲堂直播 | 会展中心 | 特价专栏 | 技术快讯 | 免费试用 版权所有 生物通 Copyright© eBiotrade.com, All Rights Reserved 联系信箱: 粤ICP备09063491号

“畅读会员”点此登录查看原文链接 Open access 拉沙病毒(Lassa virus,LASV)在西非引起严重出血热,但目前尚无获批疫苗。LASV抗原设计的主要障碍在于,其唯一中和靶点糖蛋白复合物(glycoprotein complex,GPC)缺乏内在晚期结构域(late-domain)基序,无法招募宿主ESCRT(endosomal sorting complex required for transport)机制以完成颗粒释放。在此,研究人员报告一种理性设计策略:通过在LASV GPC胞质域末端附加合成的ESCRT招募盒(ESCRT-recruitment cassette),赋予其自主出芽能力。对由16个构建体组成的矩阵进行系统筛选,鉴定出先导候选VLPdEm5。该构建体整合ESCRT招募盒、优化的弗林蛋白酶(furin)切割位点以及异源H1N1跨膜-胞质域(transmembrane-cytoplasmic domain),以支持高效颗粒组装和构象中和表位的正确展示。通过脂质纳米颗粒包封的mRNA(lipid-nanoparticle-encapsulated mRNA,mRNA-LNP)递送,VLPdEm5驱动高效原位病毒样颗粒(virus-like particle,VLP)自组装,诱导快速、高滴度结合抗体,对六个主要LASV谱系具有广泛交叉反应性,并诱导强生发中心B细胞(germinal center B-cell,GC B-cell)活性和记忆T细胞(memory T-cell)应答。关键的是,VLPdEm5 mRNA-LNP在体内针对假病毒攻击提供剂量依赖性保护。该工作建立了一种有效的LASV疫苗候选,并验证了一种广泛适用于非出芽型病毒包膜蛋白的ESCRT工程化mRNA-VLP平台。 研究背景与问题:拉沙病毒(Lassa virus,LASV)在西非流行,可致重型出血热,估计每年30万–50万病例,住院重症病死率可达15%,但尚无获批疫苗或LASV特异性抗病毒药。糖蛋白复合物(glycoprotein complex,GPC)是唯一中和靶点和保护性免疫主要决定因素,其成熟三聚体构象要求严格、糖盾致密;天然GPC胞质尾缺乏晚期结构域(late-domain)基序,不能招募ESCRT(endosomal sorting complex required for transport)机制,单独表达时病毒样颗粒(virus-like particle,VLP)释放很低。VLP多价重复展示有利于B细胞受体交联;Hoffmann等已证明CEP55来源EABR(ESCRT- and ALIX-binding region)可促eVLPs。研究人员据此设计ESCRT工程化GPC VLP,并以mRNA-LNP(lipid nanoparticle-encapsulated mRNA)递送。 研究开展与意义:研究人员构建16种LASV GPC VLP构建体,筛选出VLPdEm5,整合EPM-EABR、弗林蛋白酶(furin)切割位点RRRR和H1N1 HA跨膜-胞质域(transmembrane-cytoplasmic domain,TM-CT);经体外表征、mRNA/质粒LNP制备、小鼠免疫、细胞免疫和假病毒攻击,显示其诱导体液和细胞免疫并提供剂量依赖保护。该研究建立LASV候选疫苗并验证可推广至非出芽包膜蛋白的mRNA-VLP平台。 关键技术方法(≤250字):以LASV Josiah GPC(GenBank: NP_694870.1)为基础模块化设计16种VLP构建体;用双抗体夹心ELISA(DAS-ELISA)和Western blot筛选颗粒释放;Expi293F表达、超速离心纯化,并以尺寸排阻色谱(SEC)、纳米颗粒跟踪分析(NTA)、负染透射电镜(TEM)表征;ELISA测单抗及血清结合,假病毒中和试验测NT50;体外转录(IVT)制备mRNA,微流控混合制备LNP并测粒径、PDI和包封率;雌性BALB/c小鼠免疫,流式细胞术分析脾细胞,并以表达Renilla luciferase的VSVΔG-LASV Josiah假病毒腹腔攻击和体内生物发光成像(BLI)评价保护。样本来源为雌性BALB/c小鼠。 结果:1. LASV GPC VLP构建体的设计与筛选(Design and screening of LASV GPC VLP constructs):DAS-ELISA和Western blot筛选16构建体,VLPdEm5结合活性最高(AUC 59.7%),野生型GPC很低;EPM-EABR是高效释放主因,furin位点和H1N1 HA TM-CT亦增强。 2. 先导候选VLPdEm5的体外表征(In vitro characterization of the lead candidate VLPdEm5):SEC单峰8.94 mL,NTA平均约150 nm,负染TEM见100–200 nm球形膜包被颗粒和表面刺突;ELISA显示与12.1F、25.10C、37.7H结合EC50分别0.47、0.16、0.22 μg/mL,与8.9F弱(48.08 μg/mL),S309无结合,说明保留多个构象中和表位。 3. mRNA/质粒来源VLPdEm5 LNP制剂的制备与表征(Preparation and characterization of mRNA/plasmid-derived VLPdEm5 LNP formulations):7种mRNA经凝胶见约2500 nt单一条带;mRNA-VLPdEm5的DAS-ELISA与质粒来源相当,单独GPC仅背景;mRNA-LNP粒径约100 nm、PDI 0.10、包封率94%,质粒-LNP PDI 0.27、包封率70%;LNP制剂抗原表达优于裸核酸,空LNP无。 4. VLPdEm5 mRNA-LNP诱导高水平广交叉结合抗体(VLPdEm5 mRNA-LNP elicits high-level and broadly cross-reactive binding antibody responses in mice):mRNA-LNP day28 ED50均值471,day56均值8862;质粒-LNP低剂量后结合抗体延迟出现;day70 mRNA-LNP弱中和NT50约1:30–1:70,质粒-LNP未检测到;day70血清结合六个LASV谱系GPC。 5. VLPdEm5 mRNA/质粒-LNP诱导强细胞免疫(VLPdEm5 mRNA/Plasmid-LNP elicits robust cellular immunity in mice):day70脾细胞流式显示两疫苗组GC B细胞(CD19+GL7+CD185+)频率显著高于PBS;GC-Tfh无显著增加;CD4+和CD8+中央记忆T(CD44+CD62L+)显著增加,效应记忆T呈增加趋势;GPC刺激后mRNA-LNP组CD4+TNFα+、CD4+IFN-γ+、CD8+IFN-γ+显著高于PBS,质粒-LNP组CD4+IFN-γ+显著。 6. VLPdEm5 mRNA-LNP保护小鼠免受LASV假病毒攻击(VLPdEm5 mRNA-LNP protects mice from LASV pseudovirus challenge):BALB/c小鼠(n=5)接种2或20 μg mRNA-LNP后day56腹腔挑战表达Renilla luciferase的LASV Josiah假病毒,连续6天BLI;信号day3峰值;20 μg组day1–3显著低于PBS,2 μg组仅day3显著,day4–6组间无差异;说明剂量依赖保护。 讨论与结论:讨论指出LASV为WHO优先病原且无获批疫苗,GPC糖盾和严苛构象使高滴度中和抗体难以稳定诱导,天然GPC不能自主出芽;VLPdEm5的EPM-EABR使GPC自主招募ESCRT,furin位点改善成熟,H1N1 HA TM-CT改善膜展示;mRNA-LNP可重现质粒表达与颗粒释放。体内结合抗体快速、高滴度且跨六谱系,GC B和记忆T增强,假病毒攻击呈剂量依赖保护;但中和滴度有限(NT50≈1:30–1:70),原文将此与GPC糖盾遮蔽、可及中和表位少且隐蔽、非中和表位免疫优势以及非中和抗体Fc效应和细胞免疫参与保护相关联。局限为仅用小鼠Josiah假病毒而非真病毒致死模型;广结合不等于跨谱系中和;非中和抗体与细胞免疫贡献待明确。研究结论(翻译):综上,研究人员通过在LASV GPC C端引入ESCRT招募基序并结合mRNA-LNP递送,将本身缺乏出芽能力的病毒包膜糖蛋白转化为强效、广泛交叉反应免疫原;系统优化VLP构建体进一步提高VLP产量;这些工作建立可转移框架以改善免疫原性,并为将其他出芽效率低的病毒包膜蛋白转化为自组装、免疫原性mRNA-VLP疫苗提供可转移技术策略。 打赏 展开全文 开通VIP 享海量文章 全站开放获取+解锁超过 200万篇新闻全文+每日更新 2000+篇,学术前沿动态全时追踪! 从2000到2026,27载全因有您;您的每一分支持,都给予我们无穷的动力! 公测期:打赏8元解锁30天免费阅读! 下载安捷伦电子书《通过细胞代谢揭示新的药物靶点》探索如何通过代谢分析促进您的药物发现研究 10x Genomics新品Visium HD 开启单细胞分辨率的全转录组空间分析! 欢迎下载Twist《不断变化的CRISPR筛选格局》电子书 下载《细胞内蛋白质互作分析方法电子书》 引领行业 | 聚焦麦特绘谱代谢组学整体解决方案>> 「大小鼠繁育与健康管理」指导海报,点击即可免费领取电子版或实体海报>> 揭秘单细胞测序-深入了解这项正在改变我们开展科学研究的技术>> 18,000+ 成品模型现货随取,点击下载模式生物选型指南>> 相关新闻 生物通微信公众号 生物通新浪微博 微信 新浪微博 我要投稿 搜索 国际 国内 人物 产业 热点 科普 热搜:拉沙病毒(LASV)|糖蛋白复合物(GPC)|病毒样颗粒(VLP)|ESCRT招募基序|mRNA-脂质纳米颗粒(mRNA-LNP)|体液与细胞免疫 热点排行 今日动态 | 人才市场 | 新技术专栏 | 中国科学人 | 云展台 | BioHot | 云讲堂直播 | 会展中心 | 特价专栏 | 技术快讯 | 免费试用 版权所有 生物通 Copyright© eBiotrade.com, All Rights Reserved 联系信箱: 粤ICP备09063491号

Sign In Follow US Metro Oyo govt intensifies fumigation of public spaces to prevent Ebola, others Busola Oworu November 24, 2026 Share Add as a preferred source Oyo State Government has intensified fumigation and disinfection of strategic public spaces across the state as part of efforts to prevent the spread of infectious diseases, including Ebola and Lassa fever. This was contained in a statement released by the Commissioner for Information, Prince Dotun Oyelade, who said that the Commissioner for Environment and Natural Resources, Ademola Aderinto, disclosed this during a fumigation and disinfection exercise at selected locations in Ibadan. Aderinto said the exercise was part of the ministry’s routine responsibility to maintain a healthy environment and support the government’s public health protection measures. ALSO READ: 17 APC supporters died, 27 injured in Zamfara campaign accident He said the government was taking proactive steps to guard against the possible introduction and spread of infectious diseases, stressing that it would not wait for an outbreak before taking preventive action. “Although we have not recorded any confirmed case of Ebola in Oyo State, we will not take chances or wait until there is an outbreak before putting preventive measures in place,” he said. The commissioner explained that the exercise covered several strategic public spaces beyond the Ibadan Airport, particularly locations that attract large crowds and witness considerable human movement. He listed Mapo Hall and the Ibadan Airport among the locations covered, adding that markets, public event centres and other places of public interest would also benefit from the exercise. According to him, the ministry will sustain the fumigation and disinfection programme as part of efforts to ensure that public spaces remain safe for residents, visitors and business operators. He added that the exercise would be extended to areas that host major gatherings and events to minimise environmental health risks. news.wechat_summary_zh: 时间：2026 年 11 月 24 日，奥约州政府加强了对公共场所的熏蒸和消毒，以防止埃博拉病毒和其他传染病的传播。；地点与对象：这包含在信息专员 Dotun Oyelade 亲王发布的一份声明中，他说环境和自然资源专员阿德莫拉·阿德林托 (Ademola Aderinto) 在伊巴丹选定地点的熏...；事件：奥约州政府加强公共场所熏蒸消毒，防止埃博拉、拉沙热等传染病传播。政府正在采取积极措施，防止传染病可能的引入和传播。；影响与风险：此次演习涵盖了多个战略性公共空间，包括伊巴丹机场、马波大厅和市场。政府将继续实施熏蒸和消毒计划，以确保公共场所的安全。；应对与不确定性：政府正在采取积极措施防止传染病的传播。奥约州尚未记录埃博拉确诊病例。
